events.continuity_hook: This follows the Milwaukee booking decision and keeps the family trip intact unless the connection risk now feels too high.
events.interaction_goal: Give Erin a quick keep-or-change recommendation for the outbound connection, then create a final checklist for seats, rental-car pickup, hotel check-in, family arrival timing, and weather monitoring.
events.scenario_brief: In the week before the Milwaukee family visit, Erin checks the booked Denver-to-Milwaukee one-stop itinerary, the one-night suburban hotel, and the rental-car plan. The airline has nudged the outbound connection a little tighter, the early-evening family dinner is still fixed, and the hotel has a firm same-day cancellation cutoff. She mainly needs to decide whether the current connection is still safe enough for holiday travel and make sure her spouse's seat, carry-on plan, and hotel arrival timing are aligned.

events.continuity_hook: After closing the Milwaukee family-trip details, Erin returns to a typical regional work trip with the exact training site not yet locked down.
events.interaction_goal: Build a ranked first plan for flights, hotel zones, and rental-car versus rideshare options, separating the best plan for a Davis site from the best plan for a Sacramento clinic-office site.
events.scenario_brief: Erin starts planning a Sacramento-area analyzer rollout for a veterinary group, with training sessions Tuesday and Wednesday and a possible Monday afternoon equipment handoff. The client has not decided whether the work will happen at a Davis lab or a Sacramento clinic office, so the hotel zone and ground transportation choice are still open. Denver-to-Sacramento flights have a few workable departures, but she will have one checked training case and wants enough arrival buffer if the Monday handoff becomes firm.

events.continuity_hook: This narrows the Sacramento-area plan after the client confirms both the Davis location and the Monday handoff time.
events.interaction_goal: Help Erin choose the safer outbound flight, decide between the closer Davis hotel and the amenity-heavy airport option, and settle the rental-car booking because of the training case and suburban schedule.
events.scenario_brief: The Sacramento client confirms the Davis lab and sets the Monday equipment handoff for 3:00 p.m. The most comfortable later Denver departure no longer leaves enough room for baggage pickup and the drive to Davis, while a late-morning option protects the handoff with a less convenient start to the travel day. The best Davis hotel is close to the lab and well reviewed with a pool and fitness room, but it does not list a hot tub; an airport-area suite hotel has stronger recovery amenities but adds commute time on both training mornings.

events.continuity_hook: This is a post-booking change to the Sacramento-area work trip, driven by a new client agenda item rather than a problem with the original plan.
events.interaction_goal: Compare keeping the Thursday return against shifting to a Friday afternoon return, then outline the hotel-night, rental-car, seat, and expense steps if she extends the trip.
events.scenario_brief: After Erin books the Davis trip, the client adds a Thursday late-afternoon manager roundtable at the Sacramento office and asks whether she can remain for a Friday morning workflow wrap-up. Her booked Thursday evening return would require leaving the roundtable early, while moving home Friday adds one hotel night and an extra rental-car day. The outbound, Davis hotel, and Monday handoff still work, but she needs to decide if the added client time is worth changing the return.

events.continuity_hook: This is the final risk-reduction check for the Sacramento-area rollout after the flight, hotel, car, and client schedule were chosen.
events.interaction_goal: Assess whether to keep the current outbound or move earlier, then list the final flight, baggage, hotel, rental-car, weather, and client-timing checks Erin should complete before departure.
events.scenario_brief: A few days before leaving for Davis, Erin sees rain in the Sacramento forecast and possible morning deicing delays in Denver. Her selected outbound still arrives early enough for the Monday handoff if it runs close to schedule, and the hotel and rental car remain confirmed. She wants a fast risk check rather than reopening the full plan, plus a practical packing and logistics list for the checked case, window seat, rental counter, hotel arrival, and client contacts.

events.continuity_hook: After the Sacramento rollout, Erin shifts to a personal weekend trip where comfort and weather resilience matter more than being closest to a training site.
events.interaction_goal: Compare flying versus driving at a high level, shortlist the best hotel areas for a Santa Fe weekend, and identify the date and weather decisions Erin needs before booking.
events.scenario_brief: Erin begins planning a winter long weekend in Santa Fe with her spouse after a busy stretch of work trips. They are considering either flying into Albuquerque and renting a car or driving from Denver if the mountain weather looks calm. The trip is leisure-focused, so the hotel choice matters more than usual: they want a comfortable base near the Plaza or a quieter resort-style option outside town, with good guest ratings and recovery amenities if available. Dates are flexible within a two-week window, but they want to avoid a tiring return that would make Monday work difficult.
